content.what_it_is: FUNWAVE-TVD one-way nesting/coupling boundary input, both subroutines guarded by '# if defined (COUPLING)' (L45/L344-345 and L348/L598). SUBROUTINE COUPLING_INITIAL (L53-344, history 05/01/2010 Fengyan Shi L50): verifies COUPLING_FILE exists (INQUIRE L58; missing -> STOP L64/L67), opens unit 11 (L71) and reads header, then per-boundary counts and start indices N_COUPLING_EAST/J_START_EAST (L79), WEST (L82), SOUTH/I_START_SOUTH (L85), NORTH (L88); first time level TIME_COUPLING_1 (L93, copied to TIME_COUPLING_2 L95); for each boundary with N>0 allocates U/V/Z_COUPLING_*(N,2) and reads the first U,V,Z rows in fixed FORMAT 119 '5E16.6' (L114) into slot 2, copying to slot 1 (east L98-113, west L117-132, south L134-149, north L151-167; empty boundaries consume one line L111 etc). Then maps each boundary's global start segment onto the local subdomain: PARALLEL branch (only on physical-edge ranks, n_*==MPI_PROC_NULL) computes Kstart_*/Kend_* = start+Nghost-(jjsta-1) or (iista-1) (ykchoi Jan/23/2018 correction, west L179-180, east L222-223, south L265-266, north L308-309), clips to interior [Nghost+1, Nloc-Nghost] or [.., Mloc-Nghost] with offset Kshift_* and IN_DOMAIN_* flags for partial overlap (L182-203 west and analogues) or full-span coverage (L195-199 etc); serial branch sets Kstart/Kend directly with Kshift=-(Kstart-Nghost)+1 and IN_DOMAIN=.TRUE. (west L207-210, east L251-254, south L294-297, north L337-340). SUBROUTINE OneWayCoupling (L357-597, history 04/28/2012 L353, comment L360 explains IOSTAT replaces END=): when TIME passes both time levels (L367) shifts TIME_COUPLING_1=TIME_COUPLING_2 (L368), reads next time (L371-372), then for each boundary consumes a separator line and reads next U/V/Z rows in FORMAT 119 with IOSTAT<0 -> GOTO 120 on EOF (east L376-397, west L399-424, south L426-451, north L453-478; slot-2-to-1 shifts at L379-381, L404-406, L431-433, L458-460); label 120 CONTINUE @L483; computes linear time-interpolation weights tmp2=(TIME_COUPLING_2-TIME)/MAX(SMALL,|T2-T1|), tmp1=1-tmp2 (L494-496; both ZERO before first level or when no more data L489-492); finally writes interpolated ETA/U/V into ghost cells and rebuilds fluxes HU=(Depth+ETA)*U, HV=(Depth+ETA)*V along each active in-domain boundary: west ghost columns I=1..Nghost (L507-518), east I=Iend+1..Iend+Nghost (L531-542), south ghost rows J=1..Nghost (L555-566), north J=Jend+1..Jend+Nghost (L579-590), indexing the coupling arrays with J-Nghost+Kshift_* (or I-...).
entities: all other variables (COUPLING_FILE, FILE_EXIST, N_COUPLING_*, J_START_*, I_START_*, TIME_COUPLING_1/2, U/V/Z_COUPLING_* arrays, Kstart_*, Kend_*, Kshift_*, IN_DOMAIN_*, ETA,U,V,HU,HV,Depth,tmp1,tmp2) come from USE GLOBAL (L54, L358)

offset when segment starts inside; serial @L209
continuation L510: +Z_COUPLING_WEST(...,1)*tmp2; U @L511-512, V @L513-514; east @L533-538, south @L557-562, north @L581-586

verbatim_spans.text: !    COUPLING_INITIAL is the subroutine to initialize coupling/nesting conditions
!   OneWayCoupling subroutine is used to pass coupling variables into ghost cells
!  due to some syntax changes, we use iostat rather than end=

unresolved: Cross-line: in OneWayCoupling every boundary separator line ('! east' etc.) is list-directed READ into TIME_COUPLING_2 (L376, L395, L401, L422, L428, L449, L455, L476) - the commented-out originals (L375 etc.) read the line without a variable; if the separator line is non-numeric text the read yields IOstatus>0 (error, not EOF) which is not trapped by 'IF (IOstatus < 0)', leaving TIME_COUPLING_2 undefined by that statement; the real next time was already read at L371, so these reads at best re-consume separator lines and at worst overwrite the time level

EOF handling: GOTO 120 from any partial read (L372-477) jumps past all remaining boundary reads to L483, so a truncated last record leaves slot-2 arrays partially updated while TIME_COUPLING_1 was already advanced (L368)

PARALLEL overlap test @L182-183 (and east/south/north analogues) combines '>Nghost .AND. <Nloc-Nghost+1' terms with .OR. in a way that treats one-endpoint-inside as partial overlap; the full-span case is handled separately @L195-199 - boundary-case correctness at exact subdomain edges depends on these inequalities being exclusive

Ghost-cell fill loops use fixed local ghost ranges I=1..Nghost (west L508) and I=Iend+1..Iend+Nghost (east L532) etc., while coupling array index J-Nghost+Kshift_* must stay within 1..N_COUPLING_*; no explicit bounds check on the index expression
Format 119 (5E16.6) requires the nesting file rows to wrap every 5 values; declared twice (L114, L363) with the same label in different scopes
OneWayCoupling interpolates and overwrites ETA/U/V/HU/HV only in ghost cells - interior is untouched (one-way nesting); no ETA0/masking interaction in this file
